check.name: lens.design
check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

message.text: `probeConclusive` now treats exit 125 as inconclusive. `probesConclusive` is built on it, and `runStands` asks `probesConclusive` before it attaches to or copies a finished probing run. So any finished probing run that holds even one probe exiting 125 can never be reused, even when its record reads `ran` because the prober skipped that attack as it was told to. The new decision changes what 125 means for answering an attack and for reruns. It does not amend the probing-reuse decision, and it never says that one 125 probe makes the whole lens run again on every review.

evidence.snippet: Status: the maintainer ruled on 2026-11-16, in the coordinator's session, as [issue #514](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/514) records: "Whether probing or not, a lens with the same running parameters (including the fact that it is a probing lens) on the same code, should not be run again." He asked for the change to be fast-tracked, said he accepts the risk, and said the installed dependencies of the code under test need not be in the key. The issue asked for this file to supersede [the 2026-11-14 decision](2026-11-14-probing-runs-not-reused.md). The builder amends it instead: two active decisions amend it, and the decision index refuses an amendment of a superseded decision, so superseding it would mean superseding both of them and the decision that amends one of those.

One function, `runStands` in `packages/pipeline/src/review.ts`, decides whether a finished run may stand for its lens in a later review. The copy asks it of every run, and the attach, in its read ahead and its commit, asks it of every run under `--rerun` and of every probing run otherwise. A plain repeat still attaches to a task whose lens that does not probe failed, and shows what it stored, as it always has: `--rerun` is how such a lens runs again. A probing run is new to reuse, so a plain repeat reuses one only when it stands. A run stands when both halves hold:

1. **Its record reads ran.** `runStands` asks `lensRecord`, the function that writes the lens's record, so a run whose record reads ended or failed is never reused, for any reason the record knows now or learns later: an outcome other than done, an attack the prober left unanswered, a findings cap, lost standards, or a budget's end at a level that does not count it. The record then goes through `plan.mark`, which fails a run that finished on a model the plan refuses, so `runStands` also asks the same `refused` question of every model the run was judged by: the one it finished on and, when its prober runs on the level's own tier, the prober's.
2. **Every probe it tried ended conclusively.** `probesConclusive` in `packages/pipeline/src/probing.ts` reads the prober's `ProbingDocument`: each `run_probe` call's ID in `attempts` must have a stored result, and that result must be conclusive by `probeConclusive`, the definition the rerun task uses. A probe the sandbox refused leaves an attempt with no result; one that timed out, was cut or was ended by a signal says nothing. A run holding one is not reused, and the next review of that head plans and probes again.

Three reviews found the three cases this rule closes, each a place where reuse asked a narrower question than the record. Codex's adversarial review at `b4dd5bef` found a prober that failed over to a fallback the committed tier refuses: the record failed the lens, but the copy and `-- [cut at 2 KiB]

- A stored rerun that failed or passed stands for every repeat review of its head. One that timed out, was cut or ended by a signal runs again on a repeat review, as a refused one does, since its cause may have passed.

probes: `${probeIs} To change the code, copy the checkout into a folder under TMPDIR and work in the copy, leaving out node_modules and anything that is neither a file, a folder nor a link, such as the device the sandbox puts where a file such as .npmrc might hold a credential. Give the copy a node_modules directory of its own holding a link to each top-level entry of the checkout's, since a test runner writes beside its dependencies, and point any link to one of the repository's own packages at that package in the copy. Run the test file the attack names on the unchanged copy first, then change the behaviour the attack names, one line where one line will do, and run it again. Run the test runner through node, as node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs --run <file> runs Vitest, since npx is not on PATH. Exit 1 when the test passes with the behaviour changed, the attack's failing outcome, since no test fails for it; exit 0 when it fails, its passing outcome. When the test already fails on the unchanged copy, the probe cannot show whether the test covers the behaviour: print what it printed, exit 125, and report no finding. Print the line you changed and what the test printed each time, since the output is the evidence. A probe that only restates the claim, or fails for a reason of its own such as a syntax error, shows nothing.`,

"Run a probe for one attack of the plan: a Node ES module, run as probe.mjs with your files beside it, in a read-only checkout of the head with no network. Exit 0 for the attack's passing outcome, 125 when the probe cannot test its attack, and any other non-zero code when it shows the defect. Returns the probe's ID, its exit, and its output.",

explanation.what: `probeConclusive` now treats exit 125 as inconclusive. `probesConclusive` is built on it, and `runStands` asks `probesConclusive` before it attaches to or copies a finished probing run. So any finished probing run that holds even one probe exiting 125 can never be reused, even when its record reads `ran` because the prober skipped that attack as it was told to. The new decision changes what 125 means for answering an attack and for reruns. It does not amend the probing-reuse decision, and it never says that one 125 probe makes the whole lens run again on every review.
explanation.whatToDo: Keep 'conclusive for reuse' separate from 'shows something'. For example, let `probesConclusive` (the reuse half of `runStands`) accept a probe that ran to its end with exit 125, and keep `probeConclusive` excluding 125 only for answering attacks and for confirming claims. Or amend the reuse decision on purpose, state the cost, and have the maintainer rule on it.
explanation.whyHere: The ACTIVE base decision `2026-11-16-finished-probing-runs-are-reused.md` records the maintainer's ruling that a lens with the same running parameters on the same code "should not be run again". It makes an exception only for probes that "timed out, was cut or was ended by a signal" or were refused. The base probe-reruns decision gives the reason for that exception: "since its cause may have passed". A 125 is not a passing condition. The tests lens's wording tells its prober to exit 125 whenever the test already fails on the unchanged copy, and this change lets the tests lens probe. `run_probe`'s new description, offered to every probing lens including `trust-boundary-probes` in Melian's own rounds, invites 125 too. So the exception's shape is kept, but its reason no longer holds: a cause that will not pass now forces a full re-plan and re-probe on every repeat review of an unchanged head.

properties.failureScenario: A pull request is reviewed with a tests-derived probing lens, or with `trust-boundary-probes`. For attack 2, the prober runs a probe. The probe finds that the test already fails on the unchanged copy and exits 125, as `packages/core/src/probing-wording.ts:40` tells it to. The prober then skips attack 2 with a reason, as the reminder asks. The lens record reads `ran` and the round reads clean. The finisher then records a dismissal and repeats the round to publish the verdict. Nothing has changed: same head, same request key. At review.ts:1448, `probesConclusive` returns false because `probeConclusive({exitCode:125,...})` is false at probing.ts:357. So the repeat neither attaches nor copies. It plans and probes the whole lens again, paying $0.65 to $1.69 and about four minutes per the base decision's own figures. Because probing is not deterministic, the repeat can report a finding the first run did not, and block a pull request that had just read clean. That is the case the reuse ruling exists to prevent. The same happens on every later repeat of that head, because the test still fails before the change.
